title: Clean Env Runner
user: Developers testing workflows locally who need to reproduce a run with an explicit, reviewable environment instead of accidentally inheriting credentials and settings from their shell.

evidence.quote_or_summary: A developer describing a modern terminal/IDE/agent setup asks what others use and highlights debugging across several local tools.
Act users request host execution without inheriting every parent-process environment variable so local workflow tests do not expose unrelated credentials and session state.

recurrence: The request comes from both day-to-day multi-tool development and local Actions emulation; accidental ambient configuration makes a test irreproducible and can leak credentials.
current_workaround: Open a fresh shell, hand-write env -i commands, maintain several .env files, or hope that CI behaves like a developer laptop.
incumbents_and_gap: direnv, dotenvx, Act, and 1Password inject variables, but they do not make an allowlisted environment and its provenance a repeatable test artifact across arbitrary commands.
smallest_useful_product: A CLI wrapper with declarative allowlists, secret-name placeholders, environment diff previews, and a scrubbed run receipt.
success_measure: At least 80% of pilot runs reproduce after a clean-shell restart, with no variable outside the manifest visible to the child process.
constraints: Never log secret values; use OS keychain references only; account for Windows, macOS, and Linux process-environment differences.
why_distinct: The product is an explicit environment boundary and receipt, not another dotenv loader.
